summary: Use a visibly authored projected-display metaphor to reveal layers or selection, without claiming a real optical hologram.
objective: Layer depth and active selection remain legible without relying on bloom, and the view identifies any metaphorical projection effect.
intent_signals: Present a luminous layered diagram without claiming real holography
example_prompts: Show a holographic-style service map with stable node identities and independently pausable scan decoration.

principles: Use a visibly authored projected-display metaphor to reveal layers or selection, without claiming a real optical hologram.
implementation: Simplify internal layers and add a clear boundary or display base where useful; choose which edges carry the main shape.
Use restrained luminous accents, transparent-looking fills and a darker neutral reference; preserve contrast for labels and selected objects.
Favor a slow orbit or deliberate layer reveal; decorative scan motion should be independently pausable and should not generate model state.

Author the projection as additive emissive - new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color: 0x3fd0ff, transparent: true, opacity: 0.45, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false}) - and add UnrealBloomPass at threshold 1.0, strength 0.6, radius 0.8 over a #04070f to #0b1c33 gradient background.

Scroll a 2-on / 2-off horizontal scanline mask at 0.12 screen-heights per second across the emissive pass, then verify legibility with bloom disabled; if layers stop separating, raise material opacity rather than bloom strength.
observable_checks: Layer depth and active selection remain legible without relying on bloom, and the view identifies any metaphorical projection effect.

defaults.rationale: A hologram is light drawn over darkness, so the palette keeps every physical surface below 12% saturation and gives the two emissive hues, cyan and violet, the entire colour budget on a dark gradient sky rather than flat black. Bloom sits at strength 0.6 with threshold 1.0 because that is enough to read as glow while the additive, depthWrite-false material still carries the layer separation on its own - the record's own check is that the image survives with bloom switched off.

values.value_structure: 75/15/10 dark/mid/light; the emissive lines are the only elements above 0.7 luminance
values.saturation_rule: two emissive hues only; every physical surface stays <= 12% saturation so the projection reads as light rather than as paint

key.note: projector base uplight, decay 2, distance 4 m

lights.ratio: emissive-dominant: the practical uplight contributes roughly one tenth of the emissive pass, and the image must still read with bloom disabled

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: emissive or MeshBasicMaterial with blending AdditiveBlending, transparent true, depthWrite false, opacity 0.35-0.6; the projector base stays opaque and physically lit so the hologram has something to sit on

values.signature_technique: a 2-on / 2-off horizontal scanline mask scrolling at 0.12 screen-heights per second over the emissive pass, plus a 0.35-opacity additive ground reflection under the projector base
never: relying on bloom to make layers legible
reusing the hologram cyan for a data-encoded channel
opaque emissive surfaces with depthWrite left on

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.1; re-tune every intensity, fog density and bloom threshold if you change the tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with wireframe or scientific encoding while keeping data colors distinct from decorative scan colors.
